sentences.text: Date : 13/02/2024 CAV ORDER 1. Rule. Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of respondent - State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with C.R.No.11210015230083 of 2023 registered with D.C.B. Police Station, Surat City for the offence punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 201 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Yatin Oza assisted by learned advocate Mr.
Sudhanshu Jha for the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence,
the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza submits that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined investigation is already concluded and present application Kiranbhai Bharatbhai Bhanushali vs State Of Gujarat on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154090152/
1 is filed after submission of charge- sheet.

sentences.text: Learned Senior Advocate further submits that the so-called incident is occurred during the period between 21.06.2022 to 16.01.2023 and FIR is registered on 22.05.2023.
Thus, there was gross delay in registering the FIR.
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza further submits that present applicant accused is arrested on 05.07.2023 and since then he is in judicial custody.

All the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate and the entire case of the prosecution is based upon the documentary evidence and during the course of investigation, the investigating officer has collected all the documents.

It is further submitted that charge-sheet is filed and number of persons have been shown as witness and it would take considerably long time to conclude the trail considering the large number of pending cases in the concerned trial Court.

It is further submitted that the record is voluminous one and there is no flight risk at the instance of the present applicant accused as documents have been collected and produced before the Court of law.
Therefore, there is no question of tampering or hampering with the evidence available on record by the applicant accused.
Thus, considering the above stated factual aspects, applicant may be enlarged on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined bail.
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza further submits that as condition of the present applicant is pitiable one, he is residing in a rented premises.

It is further submitted that at present applicant is in jail and without prejudice to his rights and contentions, he is ready and willing to deposit Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs only) before the learned Trial Court preferably within a period of 30 days but not later than 45 days from the date of his release.
It is submitted that father of the applicant has filed an undertaking dated 05.02.2024 to the aforesaid effect before this Court.
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza has tendered the said undertaking, which is taken on record.

Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza has further submitted that applicant accused is also ready and willing to file an undertaking to the aforesaid effect before the learned Trial Court within a period of one week from the date of his release.
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza submitted that other FIRs have also been registered against the applicant accused wherein other persons have also been shown as accused persons.
It is submitted that in fact those persons are the main accused persons and at the instance of those persons, applicant has acted in a particular manner.
However, somehow, in the present case those main accused persons have not been joined as accused by the complainant.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined

Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza further submits that in those FIRs registred against the present applicant and other accused persons, applicant has already been enlarged on bail considering the role attributed to the applicant.
It is further submitted that the allegations levelled in other FIRs are by and large similar in nature.
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza, therefore, submits that considering the above stated factual aspects, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned APP Mr. Jayswal appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is further submitted that name and specific role played by the applicant accused is found out from the police papers.
Learned APP

Mr.
Jayswal further submits that applicant accused was working as Custom House Agent and as a part of business, complainant has entrusted certain work to him.

It is further submitted that applicant accused has demanded amount of customs duty as well as other expenditure from the complainant but the applicant accused has not paid the said amount of customs duty to the customs department Kiranbhai Bharatbhai Bhanushali vs State Of Gujarat on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154090152/
2

sentences.text: due to which a notice came to be issued by the customs department to the complainant and thereafter complainant came to know that the amount which he has paid to the applicant accused has not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined been deposited by him before the customs department and by way of producing forged and fabricated documents before the customs department, present applicant accused has usurped huge amount of Rs.1,34,34,458/- by way of illegal means and direct involvement of the applicant accused is found out from the police papers.
Therefore, bail application of the applicant may not be entertained.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Nandish Thackar appearing for the original complainant has objected present bail application with vehemence and submitted that complainant has put trust upon the applicant accused due to business relationship and paid the amount to the applicant accused which was demanded by him for the purpose of payment of custom duty.

It is submitted that it is an admitted position of fact that the complainant has paid the said amount in the account of the applicant accused and during the course of investigation it is also found out from the statements of the employees of the present applicant accused that at the instance of the applicant accused they had gone to the bank and withdrawn the amount from the bank and handed over to the present applicant accused.

It is submitted that total 79,20,000/- has been withdrawn by three employees of the applicant accused at the instance of the applicant accused and the said NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined amount is handed over to the applicant accused.
Therefore, present applicant accused is the person who has received the cash amount.

It is further submitted that image of the complainant is damaged in the Government Department solely on the count of ill-action on the part of the applicant accused as applicant accused has not disclosed correct facts before the department as well as complainant due to which a notice was issued by the customs department to the complainant and at that time complainant came to know that the amount paid by the complainant to the applicant for the purpose of customs duty has not been paid by the applicant.
Therefore, the complainant himself has paid the said amount to the customs department along with necessary penalty as well as interest.

It is further submitted that thereafter the customs department has also initiated proceedings and statement of the complainant came to be recorded by the officer of the customs department wherein complainant has described the entire sequence of events of incident.
The complainant has also specifically stated that as and when the amount of customs duty and other expenditure of customs department was demanded, he had already paid the said amount.
The complainant has also submitted his bank statement before the concerned customs officer.
Not only that complainant has also paid principal amount, interest as well as penalty NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined before the customs department.
But thereafter present FIR is registered.

During the course of investigation the officer of the customs department has also recorded the statement of the present applicant accused under the Customs Act and as per the settled proposition of law a statement recorded by the customs officer under Sections 107 and 108 of the Customs Act is admissible in evidence in a criminal trial.
The said report is placed on record along with an affidavit-in-reply wherein it is clearly stated that present applicant accused has accepted his guilt.
Considering the aforesaid factual aspects, bail application of the applicant may not be entertained solely on the ground that he is ready and willing to deposit an amount of Rs.20,00,000/-.

sentences.text: I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.
It is found out from the record that investigation is already concluded and present application is filed after submission of charge-sheet.
The so- called incident is occurred during the period between 21.06.2022 to 16.01.2023 and FIR is registered on 22.05.2023.

Thus,
prima facie, it appears that there was delay in registering the FIR.
The applicant accused is arrested on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined 05.07.2023 and since then he is in judicial custody.

All the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate and the entire case of the prosecution is based upon the documentary evidence and during the course of investigation, the investigating officer has collected all the documents.
The trial will take its own time.

Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza has submitted that without prejudice to his rights and contentions, applicant is ready and willing to deposit Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs only) before the learned Trial Court preferably within a period of 30 days but not later than 45 days from the date of his release.
An undertaking filed by the father of the appoilcant accused to the aforesaid effect is also tendered on record.

As submitted by learned Senior Advocate Mr. Oza, the applicant shall have to file an undertaking to the aforesaid effect before the learned Trial Court within a period of one week from the date of his release.

Thus, considering the above stated factual aspects, I am inclined to consider this application.
7.

This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19644/2023 CAV ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined in (2022)10 SCC 51.
8.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
9.

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
11. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
12. The present application stands allowed accordingly.
Rule is made absolute.
